title: Prevent rapid circuit flips during capacity spikes: reopen-debounce and regional rejoin policy (hotfix)
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: production incident INC-2026-02-14 showed repeated circuit flips in regional slowpaths as capacity returned after an outage. Rapid reopen/close oscillation caused request churn and SLO violations for a subset of tenants. Root cause: when nodes rejoin, transient latency spikes and KV-cache warmups briefly increase error/latency signals that the circuit controller treats as persistent failures. This PR introduces two coordinated mitigations: 1) a configurable reopen debounce (default 5s) that prevents immediate reopen attempts when a circuit has just tripped, allowing validation of sustained healthy signals; 2) a regional rejoin policy that places newly-joined nodes into a short 'quiesce' window where they are eligible for gradual traffic reintroduction with exponential backoff and jitter. Changes are behind a feature-flagged rollout and include additional telemetry spans and metrics to surface reopen attempts, debounce firings, and rejoin progression. This PR is a hotfix: it targets main and is intended for quick rollout with an immediate canary followed by staged increase. The description below summarizes commits, changed areas, tests, CI behavior, review comments, and merge details.

release_notes: Hotfix: Adds reopen-debounce to circuit controller and a regional rejoin policy to prevent reopen/close oscillation during capacity recovery. Default feature-flag off for Dedicated/Private. Improves SLO stability during rapid node rejoin events; exposes new metrics for observability: reopen_attempts_total, reopen_debounce_fired_total, rejoin_stage_gauge. Rollout: canary in one region then staged ramp.
